newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Anadolu Cam to raise sales by 60 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turk Anadolu Cam to raise sales by 60 pct in 1997.

text.p: Turkish glass container producer Anadolu Cam Sanayii A.S. wants to increase its turnover by 60 percent in real terms this year, over an expected four trillion lira in 1996, a company official said.

"We will raise our total sales to 198,000 tonnes in 1997, against 118,307 tonnes in 1996 and this will increase the turnover by 60 percent in real terms," Yildirim Canberk, the general manager of the company, told Reuters.
Total sales of the company stood at 1.8 trillion lira and net profits at 237 billion lira in 1995.
Company shares listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange traded at 2,900 lira on Monday, against 2,600 lira at Friday's close.

Canberk said they almost met last year's budget targets despite negative market conditions which he listed as rising disposable PET bottle and can consumption in Turkey and the inability to raise their prices due to lower demand despite increasing costs.
"The number of the glass container producers in Saudi Arabia rose to nine in the last four years from previous three plants which also negatively affected our export markets," he added.
Despite the negative conditions, Anadolu Cam decided to increase its annual output capacity by 100 percent to 250,000 tonnes in 1997.
"Last year, we installed a $70 million worth third oven which will be operational in February," Canberk said.
One of the two old ovens in the plant is undergoing revision to expand its capacity to 220 tonnes per day from 150 tonnes by late April.
"So we will be able to produce at full capacity in May," Canberk said.
The company's 1996 exports were 12,000 tonnes or $4 million, short of the 20,000-tonne or $7-million targets because of growing competition in the Middle Eastern markets.
Nevertheless, Anadolu Cam put a disputed export target of 40,000 tonnes for 1997 by focusing on new markets like east Europe, Central Asian republics and possibly Iraq, Canberk said.
He added that the company developed a light-weight, one-litre bottle for the Coca Cola Company and it was approved by the Coca Cola headquarters in Atlanta in 1996.

Main shareholders of Anadolu Cam are Turkiye Is Bankasi A.S., Turkey's leading private bank with a 24.22 percent stake and Turkiye Sise Cam Fabrikalari A.S., Turkey's leading glass producing group with 39.89 percent.
The company reported 2.77 trillion lira of turnover and 462 billion lira of net profits in the first nine months of 1996, up from 1.49 trillion and 202 billion, respectively in the same 1995 period.
